grades.quote: In addition to the above atomic sequence of operations, the `AM{SWAP/ADD}_DB.{B/H}` instruction also implements the data barrier function.
grades.reason: The passage covers LoongArch atomic AM instructions. It separates the atomic read-modify-write behavior from the ordering behavior. Only the _DB variants also act as a data barrier, so a plain atomic AM instruction gives atomicity without that ordering. That is a useful part of the answer: an atomic lock may still need a barrier or a _DB form to order critical-section accesses. It doesn't mention locks or critical sections, and it doesn't say outright that the non-_DB forms lack ordering. That conclusion is inferred.
